```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

The Giotto Suite is a set of packages around one object, the `giotto` object:
GiottoClass defines it, Giotto analyses it, GiottoVisuals plots it, GiottoDisk
keeps it on disk and GiottoLens explores it interactively. GiottoConnect is
where the Suite meets everything outside it. It has three roles.

![GiottoConnect links the giotto object to other ecosystems, other software and external tools](figures/giottoconnect_roles.svg){width=100%}

## 1. Other ecosystems

Objects built in Seurat, scanpy/squidpy or Bioconductor convert to Giotto, and
back:

| Ecosystem | To Giotto | From Giotto |
|---|---|---|
| Seurat | `seuratToGiotto()` | `giottoToSeurat()` |
| AnnData (`.h5ad`) | `anndataToGiotto()` | `giottoToAnnData()` |
| SpatialExperiment / SpatialFeatureExperiment | `spatialExperimentToGiotto()` | `giottoToSpatialExperiment()` |
| SpatialData | `spatialdataToGiotto()` | |

```{r}
g <- seuratToGiotto(seurat_object)
g <- anndataToGiotto("sample.h5ad", source = "project_dir") # GiottoDisk-backed
spe <- giottoToSpatialExperiment(g)
```

Seurat, AnnData and SpatialExperiment conversions run on one *mapping engine*.
A mapping file describes where each part of an object (counts, metadata,
coordinates, polygons, reductions, networks, images) lives in the other
ecosystem. The engine looks at the structure of the input, picks the mapping
that fits, and applies it. A new version of Seurat or scanpy that keeps the
structure needs no change; a new structure needs a new mapping file, not a new
function.

Every conversion records what it did. `mappingProvenance()` lists the mapping,
what each part was read from, and what could not be carried over.
`readbackCheck()` compares the result with the input, part by part.
[Converting Seurat, AnnData and SpatialExperiment objects](converting_to_giotto.html)
walks through each of them.

## 2. Other software

The same converters write the files and objects other software reads:

- `giottoToAnnData()` writes an `.h5ad` in scanpy's layout, without python, for
  scanpy, squidpy and other AnnData-based tools.
- `giottoToSpatialExperiment()` gives a SpatialExperiment or a
  SpatialFeatureExperiment for Bioconductor packages and their plots.
- `createBentoAdata()` builds the AnnData Bento works on.

GiottoLens, the Suite's interactive viewer, is a core Suite package of its own
and works on the `giotto` object directly.

## 3. External tools

Published methods run on a `giotto` object, and their results are stored in it
like any Giotto result:

| Tool | What it does | Function |
|---|---|---|
| Banksy | spatially informed embedding and clusters | `runBanksy()` |
| BayesSpace | spatial clustering of spot data | `runBayesSpace()` |
| CellChat | cell-cell communication | `runCellChat()` |
| nnSVG | spatially variable genes | `runNnSVG()` |
| ONTraC | niche trajectories | `runONTraC()` |

```{r}
g <- runBanksy(g, lambda = 0.8)
g <- runNnSVG(g)
```

The tool's own package is needed only when it runs. Python tools (ONTraC) are
installed into a managed environment the first time they run; no conda is
needed.

Each tool is a thin wrapper: GiottoConnect passes the data, runs the original
implementation and stores the results. The paper is shown the first time a
tool runs in a session, and `objCitations()` lists the papers of every method
used on an object:

```{r}
objCitations(g)
```

[Principles](principles.html) describes the rules every connection follows,
and how to add one.
